🌍 #SDG2: Zero Hunger

How can high-yield agriculture support climate-smart policy? A PNAS study examines its potential to reduce land-use emissions, offering insights for progress toward the #GlobalGoals.

Read the article: https://ow.ly/OJ6w50ZV4jg

posts.author_name: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
posts.text: Researchers have identified various potential climate “tipping points,” but some, such as the collapse of the Greenland Ice Sheet, get most of the attention, while others, such as the abrupt thawing of boreal permafrost, are less studied. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/gy7a50ZV4Yj

posts.author_name: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
posts.text: The Ecology of Segregation in Cities Special Feature examines how segregation shapes urban environments—from access to nature to exposure to environmental hazards—and highlights pathways toward more equitable, resilient, and sustainable cities. Read now: https://ow.ly/aQNk50ZV45p

posts.author_name: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
posts.text: The European spiny water flea has reduced the diversity of native zooplankton by over 50%. A study finds it had been present in Canada for at least a century before first reports in the 1980s—and it may not have been introduced by humans. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/lkRK50ZV1nw

posts.text: Forest fragmentation increases local temperatures in temperate and tropical zones and has a stronger effect on local temperature than overall forest cover, according to a study of high-resolution remote-sensing data from around the world. In PNAS: https://ow.ly/QZjT50ZUyMj
